correctness.rationale: For any fixed-point-free cyclic complement action, the second commutator condition is automatic when the second complement coordinate is trivial and otherwise equivalent to ordinary commutation; this yields probability (a+m-1)/(am). The order-three complement elements have vanishing additive norm, and a fixed-point-free automorphism of order three forbids nonzero 3-torsion in the finite abelian kernel; this yields (2a+1)/(am). The explicit prime-power tower makes p3 approach 2/m from above and p2Engel approach 1/m, forcing f(2/m)<=1/m by monotonicity. Nine complete small finite-group enumerations agree.

value.rationale: The pointwise upper restriction on every possible universal monotone comparison answers a naturally motivated quantitative sharpness question left by the recent existence theorem. It rules out f(2/3)>1/3 and supplies barriers at an infinite set accumulating at zero, with explicit asymptotic witnesses. This is not presented merely as a routine group probability count or an optimal universal f construction.
